title: Playing under Celestin with Armstrong, and lending his horn to Bunk Johnson
summary: He played in the Tuxedo parade band with Louis Armstrong, loaned his instrument to Bunk Johnson for a Royal Garden dance, and listened to Storyville bands to learn from trumpeters.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well, yeah, they had more work than they had musicians for the work. See? We had plenty of work to do, but a little money. And I guess it was that we had with all kinds of business then. Plenty of work you had to do with money. But that gave me, what I said, it gave you a chance to play with these brothers. I played with Louis Armstrong in the Tuxedo Band, Parade Band. That was with Papa Celestein. I know you knew him. Oh yeah, I know him. It was his band. I played with Hank Heath and Louis Armstrong. See, I played the Tracking and Thurie. He and Louis, he was a leader. And Louis was playing solo. And then... That was the last band. Yeah. And then on another occasion, they had the Royal Garden. They used to have a dance up there every Sunday night. And on one occasion I had played the parade that day, and didn't have anything to do that night in the music line. So the man had the job in charge. I guess you know his name too. His name was Willie Johnson. Bunk, they used to call him. Bunk Johnson. So he asked me if I would rent Louis Mahon since I wasn't playing that night. Rent Louis Mahon so he could play a job for him. So I told him, well I'll do better than that. I let him use it. And I was a city of joy, you know. I was in love with music that much as sitting around there and enjoying the playing, see. So that's why I got real, you know, good acquainted with Louis on that night. And you knew Bunk, huh? Yeah. Yeah, I knew him. Set on a job with him for, when he was playing what they called Storyville at that time, playing on a job there. I was sitting on a job there, sitting on a job with him, listening to the band. Well I was very much interested in the band, and especially trumpet players. And anyone who could, any trumpet player who could play something, I would try and get what I could from him.
